questions.prompt: Which SDK to build first? Research users are primary audience.
questions.description: Python is recommended for research users. TypeScript for frontend integrations. CLI for power users.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Python first, then TypeScript, then CLI

options.label: Python first, then TypeScript, then CLI
TypeScript first, then Python, then CLI
CLI first, then Python, then TypeScript

questions.prompt: How should SDKs handle authentication? Current API uses session cookies (httpOnly).
questions.description: The API currently uses session cookies via browser. For SDKs, we need to support API key or token-based auth. No API key infrastructure exists yet.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Add API key auth to backend, then SDKs use API key header. Cookie auth for browser-based TypeScript SDK.

options.label: Add API key auth to backend, SDKs use Authorization header
Add bearer token endpoint, exchange cookie for token
Follow MCP pattern: PAPERVIZ_API_KEY env var (already implemented for MCP)

questions.prompt: Generate SDKs from OpenAPI spec or hand-write?
questions.description: OpenAPI spec at docs/openapi.yaml has 34 endpoints, 31 schemas. Codegen (openapi-generator, oapi-codegen) can produce clients. Hand-written allows better ergonomics, error handling, retry logic.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Codegen from OpenAPI for core client, hand-written wrapper for ergonomics (retry, polling, types)

options.label: Codegen from OpenAPI for core client, hand-written wrapper for ergonomics
Fully hand-written for maximum control and ergonomics

questions.prompt: Python SDK distribution: PyPI package name, versioning, dependencies?
questions.description: Needs a unique PyPI name. Dependencies: httpx/requests, pydantic for types. Version tied to API version.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Package name: paperviz (check PyPI availability). Use httpx + pydantic. Semver matching API. MIT license.

questions.prompt: TypeScript SDK distribution: npm package name, ESM/CJS, React hooks?
questions.description: Frontend already has api.js. TypeScript SDK could replace it or be separate. Should export types from OpenAPI.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Package name: @paperviz/sdk or paperviz-sdk. ESM + CJS dual. Export TypeScript types from OpenAPI. Optional React hooks for polling.

questions.prompt: CLI commands needed? Built with which framework?
questions.description: CLI should wrap SDK. Commands: upload (PDF/text), poll status, get results, share, list, compare, import (DOI/URL). Framework: Cobra (Go) or Click (Python).
questions.recommendedAnswer: Cobra (Go) for single binary. Commands: upload, status, get, share, list, compare, import-doi, import-url, collections. Config file for API key + base URL.

options.label: Cobra (Go) - single binary, matches backend stack

questions.description: API returns snake_case error codes. SDKs should map to typed exceptions/errors with retries for rate limits (429) and transient errors (5xx).
questions.recommendedAnswer: Typed exception hierarchy per SDK. Automatic retry with exponential backoff for 429/5xx. Configurable retry policy. Error codes as constants/enums.

questions.prompt: Include polling helpers for async document processing?
questions.description: Document creation returns 201 with status=processing. Callers must poll GET /api/documents/{id} every 2+ seconds until complete. SDK should provide convenience method.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Yes - built-in waitForCompletion(pollInterval, timeout) with callbacks for progress

options.label: Yes - built-in waitForCompletion with progress callbacks
Yes - simple poll loop, no callbacks

questions.prompt: How to test SDKs? Mock server? Integration tests against real API?
questions.description: Need unit tests for each SDK method, integration tests against test instance. Can use Prism (OpenAPI mock) or recorded responses.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Unit tests with mocked HTTP. Integration tests against local dev server. Generated contract tests from OpenAPI.
